question.problem:
Which of the following products is the LU factorization of a matrix $A?$

I. $A=[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 0 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}]$

II. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 3 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}5 & 0 \\ 0 & -1\end{aligned}]$

III. $A=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ -8 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}-2 & 1 \\ 4 & 3\end{aligned}]$

current_example.worked_solution:
Remember that in the LU factorization of a matrix $A,$ we write $A=LU$ where the matrix $L$ is a unit lower triangular matrix (a lower triangular matrix that has only $1$'s on the main diagonal) and the matrix $U$ is an upper triangular matrix:

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14145468/assets/de1a26eb5d3719e0f216b4f0c3373ba49805932d3e173405023bdbf4099178fe.svg)

With that in mind, let's inspect each product in turn.

- The first product is in $LU$ form because the left matrix is a unit lower triangular matrix, and the right matrix is an upper triangular matrix.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14145468/assets/97d237664b0e5ee2453e48de57346f3ae6e814eb58b249582499acfbf0693561.svg)

- The second product is *not* in $LU$ form. Although the left matrix is a lower triangular matrix, it is not a *unit* lower triangular matrix because it does not have $1$'s on the diagonal.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14145468/assets/fabd85e7a602e06f5e1565c62f42e898ce8b0be047cee7096ec7519ad5f04cfa.svg)

- The third product is *not* in $LU$ form because the matrix on the right is not an upper triangular matrix, as it has a non-zero entry below the diagonal.
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/foundations/14145468/assets/a8b11897df4622d75409218fe983bbd3fd761d0ec159d8404e4062eaff198675.svg)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."
